source.title: The Two Regimes of Deep Network Training

record.file_problem: None noted; the supplied text contains the paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures how learning-rate and momentum choices affect training loss and test accuracy, using a different setup from the listed versions. It does not test random-label memorization, width, convolutional bias, adaptive optimizers, batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized-example removal.
record.gate_note: Reports its own training-loss and test-accuracy results for learning-rate and momentum settings and a two-stage schedule. Results cited from prior work, including large-batch generalization, are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests learning-rate and momentum effects and proposes a two-stage schedule. It does not test any specified claim version. Batch-size and sharpness explanations are discussed without corresponding measurements. Appendix Figure 13 includes AdamW in the second phase, but examines first-phase momentum equivalence rather than establishing the tuning and matched optimizer comparison described by V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors argue that large-step training contributes generalization, whereas small-step training alone reduces loss quickly but generalizes poorly. With learning-rate compensation, first-phase momentum has little observable benefit; stronger second-phase momentum can improve accuracy. Their two-stage schedule matches or exceeds the selected reference at some transition epochs. They suggest second-order methods as future second-phase candidates rather than demonstrating their performance.
record.recipe_differences: Studies learning-rate and momentum regimes and a two-stage schedule; it does not reproduce the original methods named in the claim versions. Uses VGG-13-BN on CIFAR-10 for most experiments and ResNet-18 on ImageNet for the schedule comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy changes with learning rate and momentum; the reported momentum effects depend on the training phase and corresponding learning-rate choice. The two-stage schedule's performance is shown as a function of transition epoch.

fits_no_version.finding: Large-step and small-step training differ in training-loss behavior and the benefit of momentum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Momentum accelerates loss reduction in the small-step regime; in the large-step regime its benefits can be reproduced by adjusting learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Learning-rate compensation produces similar accuracy curves across momentum settings; changing second-phase momentum and learning rate raises mean accuracy from 88.76% to 89.94%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The effect of SGD momentum on test accuracy depends on step size and training phase.

fits_no_version.finding: A two-stage schedule matches or exceeds the reference accuracy for at least one tested transition epoch on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Separately configured training phases can yield competitive image-classification accuracy with a two-stage schedule.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 13 reports nearly identical means with and without first-phase momentum across three second-phase algorithms: 88.76%/88.74%, 89.94%/90.00%, and 88.80%/88.79% for the AdamW panel.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compensating first-phase momentum with learning rate preserves accuracy across the tested second-phase algorithms.

record.problems: Several test-accuracy results are presented only in figures without numerical values in the text. ImageNet transition points were hand picked because the experiments were expensive; learning rates and momentum values were hand picked for ImageNet. The authors note that they could not identify a sharp boundary between the two regimes.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results left out. Cited results from other studies were excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD performance under an established tuning protocol. Figure 13's second-phase AdamW results do not establish this comparison or its tuning conditions.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that change their accuracy penalty.
Dropout interventions and their interactions with training-set size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Measured magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and comparison with other measures.
Identification and removal of memorized examples compared with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: Generalization accuracy by itself does not test these specific versions. The sharp-minimum explanation is not accompanied by magnitude-aware sharpness measurements. The full-gradient appendix investigates momentum dynamics, without a fixed-epoch batch-size generalization comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep past interpolation on natural labels.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers compared with SGD or momentum SGD.
Batch-size effects and adaptations under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects and its interaction with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness comparisons and gap ranking.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: VGG-13-BN
rows.operation_detail: Trained with three momentum values at learning rate η = 0.1 in the large-step regime for 50 epochs; training loss measured.
rows.value: The largest µ value yields the worst solution; loss evolution is noisy.
rows.note: The result concerns optimization loss and does not measure a training-test generalization gap.
rows.check: Accurately describes an optimization result, but training loss alone measures none of the claim versions.

rows.subject: VGG-13-BN
rows.operation_detail: Trained with three momentum values at learning rate η = 0.001 in the small-step regime for 50 epochs; training loss measured.
rows.value: Final loss decreases as momentum increases; loss decreases almost at each epoch.
rows.note: The result concerns optimization loss and does not measure a training-test generalization gap.
rows.check: Accurately describes an optimization result, but training loss alone measures none of the claim versions.

rows.subject: VGG-13-BN
rows.operation_detail: Swept learning rate for three momentum values using SGD; measured test accuracy.
rows.value: The three curves are described as surprisingly similar, shifted by momentum; reductions in momentum appear compensated by increasing learning rate.
rows.note: Text describes the trend; exact accuracy values are figure-only.
rows.check: The reported learning-rate/momentum equivalence is outside all versions; observed is not a state for any specified version.

rows.subject: VGG-13-BN
rows.operation_detail: Trained with the best learning rate selected for each momentum value; measured training loss for 50 epochs.

conditions.value: best performing for each momentum value

rows.value: No evidence that convergence was improved; all reach very similar losses at the end of training.
rows.note: This is a training-loss outcome, not a test-error or gap measure.
rows.check: Figure 5 identifies momentum values as 0, 0.9 and 0.99, rather than 0, 0.5 and 0.9. Appendix C.4 is internally inconsistent, but its search ranges also identify 0, 0.9 and 0.99. The optimization outcome bears on no version.

rows.subject: VGG-13-BN
rows.operation_detail: Compared two phase-one settings, with and without momentum, while keeping phase two fixed; distributions of test accuracies over training runs reported.
rows.measure: Best test accuracy; reported means over distributions
rows.note: Authors state the distributions are the same for a fixed second phase.
rows.check: The 88.76% versus 88.74% comparison concerns first-phase momentum, outside all versions. Its absent state cannot be assigned to a specified version.

rows.subject: VGG-13-BN
rows.operation_detail: Compared two phase-two settings after a fixed phase one; distributions of test accuracies over training runs reported.
rows.measure: Best test accuracy; reported means over distributions
rows.note: Authors state the more aggressive momentum with an appropriate learning-rate change outperforms the classic parameters on average.
rows.check: The 88.76% versus 89.94% comparison changes learning rate and momentum within SGD; it does not compare adaptive methods with SGD.

rows.subject: VGG-13-BN
rows.operation_detail: Compared two-stage schedule with and without first-phase momentum against a three-stage reference schedule across transition epochs; test accuracy plotted.

conditions.value: two-stage, with or without momentum in phase one

rows.note: Text says the proposed schedule outperforms or matches the three-stage schedule for at least one transition epoch; precise values are figure-only.
rows.check: This is the study's proposed schedule compared with a reference method, outside all versions. Section 4.2 supplies the qualitative outcome despite unavailable exact plotted values.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Compared two-stage schedule with a three-stage reference schedule across selected transition epochs; test accuracy plotted.
rows.note: Text says the proposed schedule outperforms or matches the three-stage schedule for at least one transition epoch; precise values are figure-only.
rows.check: Appendix C.8 says the ImageNet reference accuracy was taken from torchvision documentation, rather than measured in a matched reference run. This proposed-method comparison bears on no version and should not be retained as a qualifying claim-test row.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
